related_questions.question: What triggers an IRS criminal investigation?

text_blocks.snippet: An IRS criminal investigation is typically triggered by evidence of willful tax fraud or other criminal violations of tax law, such as tax evasion, money laundering, or structuring transactions to avoid reporting requirements. These investigations are handled by the IRS Criminal Investigation (CI) division, which is the law enforcement arm of the IRS.
snippet_highlighted_words: evidence of willful tax fraud or other criminal violations of tax law, such as tax evasion, money laundering, or structuring transactions to avoid reporting requirements

list.title: Unreported Income:
list.snippet: Significant discrepancies between reported income and other financial information, or failure to report income from various sources (e.g., freelance work, offshore accounts) can raise red flags.

list.title: Excessive Deductions or Credits:
list.snippet: Claiming deductions or credits that are not supported by documentation, or that appear to be inflated, can also trigger scrutiny.

list.title: Failure to File or Pay Taxes:
list.snippet: Repeatedly failing to file tax returns or pay taxes owed can be a strong indicator of tax evasion.

list.title: False or Fraudulent Documents:
list.snippet: Submitting false or altered documents to the IRS, or creating false entries in financial records, is a serious offense.

list.title: Offshore Tax Evasion:
list.snippet: Using offshore accounts or other methods to hide assets and income from taxation is a common area of focus for IRS CI.

list.title: Money Laundering:
list.snippet: Engaging in financial transactions designed to conceal the source of illegally obtained funds can trigger investigations.

list.title: Whistleblower Tips:
list.snippet: Information provided by informants can also lead to investigations.

list.title: Tips from other agencies:
list.snippet: Information obtained during investigations by other law enforcement agencies or from U.S. Attorneys' offices can also initiate a criminal investigation.

list.title: Suspicious Deductions or Expenses:
list.snippet: Deductions that are deemed excessive or not related to business activities can also be a trigger.

list.title: Civil vs. Criminal:
list.snippet: While many tax issues are handled through civil audits, a criminal investigation is reserved for cases where there is evidence of intentional wrongdoing and a willful attempt to evade taxes.

list.title: IRS CI vs. Other IRS Divisions:
list.snippet: The IRS Criminal Investigation (CI) division is distinct from the civil audit and collection functions of the IRS. CI agents are federal law enforcement officers with the authority to investigate and pursue criminal charges.

text_blocks.snippet: If you are concerned about a potential IRS criminal investigation, it is crucial to seek legal counsel from an experienced tax attorney as soon as possible.
